_about: Nora's online sweater store (scripts/online_store.gd; Alex, 2026-11-16: 'a computer ... as a high ticket purchase item ... orders request specific animal furs ... order frequency increases by customer satisfaction (she has a star rating) ... how quickly she fills orders since request date'). Once a computer stands in her house, orders come in on the game's clock, never running out. Each wants a sweater knitted with one wild fibre (data/wildlife.json 'fibres'), sometimes at least so many stars (Sweaters.stars_for: Common and Uncommon 1, Rare 2, Epic 3, Legendary 4). interval_hours: game hours between new orders at a 1-star and a 5-star rating (in between, along the line). max_open: how many orders can stand open at once, at 1 and 5 stars. tier_weights: how likely an order is to want each tier's fibre, at 1 and 5 stars (a better shop gets the richer customers). pay: coins for an order of that tier's fibre; bonus_per_grade: a tenth more for each grade the sweater is above the least the order asks for (as locals' requests pay); stars_extra_pay: a fifth more on an order that asks for more stars than the fibre gives by itself. stars_chance: how often an order asks for one star more than its fibre gives. expire_hours: game hours an order of that tier stays open before the customer gives up. grace: the share of that time she can take and still get five stars; after it the score falls in a line to one star at expiry. An order that expires scores expired_score. catch_up_hours: how far back the clock catches up on orders missed (a night's sleep; a computer sold and bought back days later starts fresh rather than with a pile of old orders). The rating is the average of the last 'window' scores (a new shop starts at start_rating, counted as one score); 'window' keeps it able to climb back. Payment comes the morning after she fills an order (Game.day_started): the parcel goes in the morning post. The computer's price is in data/furniture.json. Balance (data/economy.json '_about_balance'): a plain sweater fetches 70 to 90c and a local's fibre request 180 to 250c, so the store wins on how many orders come, not on a big premium per sweater; what she can fill is held back by how fast the wild coats grow back. Every number and line is a draft until Alex approves it.
